Iraklis B.C.|Iraklis Thessaloniki]] | years18 = 2021–2022 | team18 = [[Manama Club (basketball)|Al Manama]] | years19 = 2022–2024 | team19 = [[Al-Ahli Jeddah (basketball)|Al-Ahli]] | years20 = 2024 | team20 = Al Manama | years21 = 2024–present | team21 = Al-Ahli | highlights = * [[Bahraini Premier League (basketball)|Bahraini League]] champion (2022) * Bahraini Cup winner (2022) * French [[LNB Pro A Best Scorer]] ([[2018-19 Pro A season|2019]]) * [[All-NBA Development League Team|All-NBA D-League Third Team]] (2016) * [[NBA Development League All-Star Game|NBA D-League All-Star]] (2014) | letter = e }} '''Devin Maurice Ebanks''' (born October 28, 1989) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Al-Ahli Jeddah (basketball)|Al-Ahli Jeddah]] of the [[Saudi Basketball League]]. The [[Forward (basketball)|forward]] was selected 43rd overall by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in the [[2010 NBA draft]]. He played [[college basketball]] for two seasons at [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia University]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nbadraft.net/2010mock_draft |title=2010 Mock Draft |publisher=NBADraft.net |access-date=April 2, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120315163707/http://nbadraft.net/2010mock_draft |archive-date=March 15, 2012 |url-status=dead }} ==High school career== As a sophomore at [[Bishop Loughlin Memorial High School]] in [[Brooklyn]], New York, Ebanks averaged 18 points, six rebounds and 1.3 assists per game. In his junior season, at [[St. Thomas More School (Connecticut)|St. Thomas More School]] in [[Connecticut]], he averaged 23 points, five rebounds, four assists and three steals. In his senior season, Ebanks recorded an average of 23 points, 10 rebounds and 5 assists per game. He scored over 1,000 points in his two seasons at St. Thomas More. Ebanks received various honors while a prep player in high school. These honors included the [[Michael Jordan|Jordan Brand Classic All-Star Game]] in New York, playing [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] basketball, and being one of 30 players selected for the 2007 USA Basketball Development Festival at the [[Olympics|U.S. Olympic]] Training Center in [[Colorado Springs, Colorado]]. While at the camp, Ebanks averaged 28.2 points and 4.8 rebounds per game. Ebanks was widely regarded as one of the top high school players in the nation by scouting services, ranking 11th overall and 13th overall in the class by Rivals.com and Scout.com, respectively.{{cite web |url=http://www.msnsportsnet.com/profile.cfm?id=101739&sport=mbball |title=West Virginia University Mountaineers |publisher=MSNsportsNET.Com |access-date=April 2, 2010 |archive-date=January 9, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100109054541/http://www.msnsportsnet.com/profile.cfm?id=101739&sport=mbball |url-status=dead }} He was being pursued by various colleges, such as [[Indiana Hoosiers|Indiana]], [[Memphis Tigers|Memphis]], [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights|Rutgers]] and [[Texas Longhorns|Texas]].{{cite web|url=http://rivalshoops.rivals.com/viewprospect.asp?pr_key=41968&Sport=2 |title=Devin Ebanks – Yahoo! Sports |publisher=Rivalshoops.rivals.com |date=May 18, 2008 |access-date=April 2, 2010 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081021101255/http://rivalshoops.rivals.com/viewprospect.asp?pr_key=41968&Sport=2 |archive-date=October 21, 2008 }} Ebanks originally signed with the Indiana Hoosiers, but was released from his letter of intent after coach [[Kelvin Sampson]] was dismissed. Ebanks signed his letter of intent with [[Bob Huggins|Bob Huggins']] [[West Virginia University]]. ==College career== At WVU, Ebanks totaled a then season-high 17 rebounds to go along with his 10 points, 3 assists, 3 steals and 2 blocks in a win over [[Cleveland State University|Cleveland State]].{{cite web|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/player/gamelog?playerId=41840&year=2009|title=Devin Ebanks West Virginia Mountaineers Game Log (2008–09)|work=ESPN.com|access-date=April 30, 2016}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} In the following 68–65 loss to #22 [[Davidson University|Davidson]] in [[Madison Square Garden]], Ebanks led the team with 17 rebounds and also had 13 points. He then followed up in the [[Duquesne University|Duquesne]] win with his third double-double: 15 points and 10 rebounds. However, his run was ended as he missed the majority of the Miami University victory with an injury. Ebanks bounced back with 9 points and 10 rebounds in the win over [[Radford University|Radford]]. In the 76–48 win over [[Ohio State Buckeyes|Ohio State]], Ebanks had 10 points and 5 rebounds. In the following win over [[Seton Hall]], Ebanks had 10 points and 9 rebounds. He played 25 minutes of the loss to #1 [[Connecticut Huskies|UConn]], however he only had 4 points and 2 rebounds; in the following loss to [[Marquette University|Marquette]] Ebanks had 8 points and 3 rebounds. In the win over [[Marshall Thundering Herd|Marshall]], he totaled 12 points and 4 rebounds, then 5 points and 10 rebounds in the win over [[South Florida Bulls|USF]]. In the following win over [[Georgetown Hoyas|Georgetown]], Ebanks had 9 points and 7 rebounds. In the loss to [[Pittsburgh Panthers|Pittsburgh]] in the [[Backyard Brawl]], Ebanks had 9 points and 5 rebounds. In the following win over [[St. John's University (New York)|St. John's]], he had 10 points and 8 rebounds. In the 69–63 loss to [[Louisville Cardinals|Louisville]], Ebanks had 14 points and 6 rebounds. As the Mountaineers lost to [[Syracuse Orangemen|Syracuse]], he recorded 9 points and 9 rebounds. In the 86–59 win over [[Providence College|Providence]], he had 13 points and 6 rebounds. In the second loss to Pittsburgh, he totaled a season-high 16 points with 7 rebounds. He followed the season-high point-performance with a double-double in the victory over [[Villanova University|Villanova]] – 16 points and 10 rebounds. In the 79–68 win over [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish|Notre Dame]], Ebanks recorded 11 points and 9 rebounds. In the following win over [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights|Rutgers]], Ebanks had another double-double with 14 points and 11 rebounds. Ebanks had a consecutive double-double in the loss to [[Cincinnati Bearcats|Cincinnati]] with 12 points and 14 rebounds. He then had 10 points and 7 rebounds in a victory over South Florida. Ebanks had his 9th double-double of his rookie campaign in the win over [[DePaul University|DePaul]] with 14 points and 14 rebounds. Ebanks ended the regular season against #6 [[Louisville Cardinals|Louisville]] with a season-high 16 points and 10 rebounds for his 10th double-double of the season. Following the 62–59 loss, Ebanks was named to the [[Big East Conference|Big East]] all-rookie team.{{cite web |url=http://westvirginia.scout.com/2/845459.html |title=Three Mountaineers Earn Big East Awards |publisher=Westvirginia.scout.com |date=March 8, 2009 |access-date=April 2, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090310181405/http://westvirginia.scout.com/2/845459.html |archive-date=March 10, 2009 |url-status=dead }} In the second round of the Big East Tournament against Notre Dame, Ebanks scored 7 points and had 5 assists to go with his season-high 18 rebounds. In the following round, defeating the #2 [[Pittsburgh Panthers]] 74–60, he had a season-high 20 points with 7 rebounds and 3 assists. In the semifinals, he led the team to overtime against #20 [[Syracuse Orangemen|Syracuse]], setting a new career-high with 22 points and he also had 6 rebounds, 3 assists and 3 steals in the 74–69 loss. Ebanks was named to the first team All-Big East Tournament squad with his average of 16 points and 10 rebounds during the tenure. However, the Mountaineers lost in the first round of the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]] to [[University of Dayton|Dayton]], 68–60, with Ebanks scoring 14 points and grabbing 12 rebounds. For his true freshman season, Ebanks averaged 10.5 points and 7.8 rebounds per game in his starting role. He had season-highs of 22 points against Syracuse and 18 rebounds against Notre Dame. He finished the year with double-point figures in 12 of his last 13 games with six double-doubles in those games.{{cite web|first=John|last=Antonik|url=http://www.wvusports.com/page.cfm?story=14405&cat=exclusives|title=Shooting it Straight|work=WVUSports.com|date=March 20, 2009 |access-date=April 2, 2010}} After some speculation, Ebanks announced he would return for his sophomore season.{{cite web|first=Bryan|last=Messerly|url=http://www.msnsportsnet.com/page.cfm?cat=netnews&story=14533|title=Men's Basketball: Ebanks to Return|work=MSNSportsnet.com|date=April 13, 2009|access-date=April 2, 2010}} ===College statistics=== {| class="wikitable" |- ! FT%!! 3P% |- | West Virginia|| 2008–09 | 35 || 30.2 || 0.8 || 0.7 || 7.8 || 2.7 || 10.5 || .470 || .700 || .125 |- | West Virginia|| 2009–10 | 34 || 34.1 || 1.1 || 0.7 || 8.1 || 2.4 || 12.0 || .457 || .770 || .100 |} ==Professional career== [[File:Devin Ebanks in 2013.jpg|thumb|left|Ebanks with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in 2013]] Ebanks declared for the [[2010 NBA draft]], and was selected 43rd overall by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. He was signed on August 12, 2010. On December 27, 2010, the Los Angeles Lakers assigned Ebanks to the [[Bakersfield Jam]] of the NBA D-League. On January 8, 2011, the Lakers recalled Ebanks from the Jam as a result of an injury sustained by [[Matt Barnes]].{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Devin-Ebanks/Summary/2302|title=Devin Ebanks Player Profile – RealGM|work=RealGM.com|access-date=April 30, 2016}} In February 2011, Ebanks fractured his leg while practicing before a game in Memphis.{{cite web|title=LAKERS FORWARD DEVIN EBANKS DIAGNOSED WITH STRESS FRACTURE OF THE LEFT TIBIA|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/110304_ebanks_fracture.html|work=NBA.com|date=March 4, 2011|access-date=April 30, 2016}} On December 23, 2011, and in his sophomore season in the NBA, Ebanks was announced the starting small forward, in place of Matt Barnes, by new Laker coach [[Mike Brown (basketball, born 1970)|Mike Brown]].{{cite web|first=Brian|last=Kamenetzky|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles/lakers/post/_/id/25098/mike-brown-names-devin-ebanks-his-starting-small-forward |title=Mike Brown names Devin Ebanks his starting small forward |work=ESPN.com |date=December 23, 2011 |access-date=December 26, 2011}} In his first game as a starter, Ebanks had 8 points, 1 rebound, and 2 assists, against the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20111225/CHILAL/gameinfo.html|title=Bulls-Lakers notebook|work=NBA.com|date=December 25, 2011|access-date=December 26, 2011}} On February 15, 2012, he was assigned with the Los Angeles D-Fenders. He was later recalled on February 26, 2012. In his sophomore season, he averaged 4 points in 16.5 minutes per game. He also played 12 of 24 games as a starter. On August 13, 2012, Ebanks re-signed with the Lakers to a one-year deal.{{cite web|title=Lakers re-sign Devin Ebanks, sign Jodie Meeks|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10745|work=InsideHoops.com|date=August 13, 2012|access-date=October 30, 2013}} On September 13, 2013, Ebanks signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Wermuth|title=MAVERICKS SIGN DEVIN EBANKS; ROSTER EXPANDS TO 19|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-devin-ebanks-roster-expands-19/|work=NBA.com|date=September 13, 2013|access-date=September 13, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004230423/http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-devin-ebanks-roster-expands-19/|archive-date=October 4, 2013|url-status=dead}} However, he was waived on October 22.{{cite web|title=Mavericks waive Renaldo Balkman, Devin Ebanks, D.J. Kennedy, Fab Melo|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14609|work=InsideHoops.com|date=October 22, 2013|access-date=October 22, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131023113919/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14609|archive-date=October 23, 2013|url-status=dead}} In November 2013, he was acquired by the [[Texas Legends]].{{cite web |title=Legends Complete Three Trades, Finalize Training Camp Roster |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/texas/legends_complete_three_trades_2013_11_04.html |work=NBA.com |date=November 4, 2013 |access-date=November 4, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131109041804/http://www.nba.com/dleague/texas/legends_complete_three_trades_2013_11_04.html |archive-date=November 9, 2013 }} On February 3, 2014, Ebanks was named to the Prospects All-Star roster for the 2014 NBA D-League All-Star Game.{{cite web|title=Eighth Annual NBA D-League All-Star Game Features 16 Players With NBA Experience |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html |work=NBA.com |date=February 3, 2014 |access-date=February 3, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140207181043/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html |archive-date=February 7, 2014 }} On February 20, he was traded to the [[Springfield Armor]].{{cite web|first=Brian|last=Kotloff|title=Five Former NBA Players Traded in Three-Team Deal|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_trade_armor_jam_legends_2014_02_20.html|work=NBA.com|date=February 20, 2014|access-date=February 20, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140301184717/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_trade_armor_jam_legends_2014_02_20.html|archive-date=March 1, 2014}} In July 2014, he joined the NBA D-League Select Team for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]]. On August 28, 2014, he signed with [[Bnei Herzliya]] of Israel for the 2014–15 season.{{cite web|title=Devin Ebanks signs with Bnei Herzliya|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/132892/devin-ebanks-signs-with-bnei-herzliya.html|work=Sportando.com|date=August 28, 2014|access-date=August 28, 2014}} On October 28, 2014, he parted ways with Herzliya after just three games, with the team citing behavioral issues.{{cite web|title=Devin Ebanks leaves Bnei Herzliya.
